question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Deafness (NPPCD) in India?

answers.text: NPPCD was launched in 2001 with the goal of eliminating all forms of deafness in India by 2020

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: NPPCD was launched in 2006 (not 2001), and its goal is to prevent avoidable deafness and reduce the burden of hearing disability — not to eliminate all deafness. Complete elimination of all deafness is not a realistic or stated programme goal.

answers.text: NPPCD was launched in 2006 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with the goal of reducing the burden of avoidable hearing loss; it mandates the 1-3-6 rule for newborn hearing screening

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. NPPCD (2006) mandates screening, early identification, and rehabilitation of hearing loss across all age groups. For neonates, the 1-3-6 rule is the programme's standard: screen by 1 month, diagnose by 3 months, fit hearing aid and begin habilitation by 6 months. This early intervention window is critical for speech and language development.

answers.text: NPPCD covers noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) only and does not address congenital or age-related hearing loss

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: NPPCD addresses all major preventable causes of hearing loss, including congenital (TORCH infections, genetic causes), childhood (ASOM, chronic otitis media, meningitis), occupational (NIHL), and age-related (presbycusis). It is a comprehensive national programme, not restricted to NIHL alone.

answers.text: NPPCD recommends universal newborn hearing screening using the 5-10-15 rule: screen at 5 days, diagnose at 10 weeks, intervene at 15 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The 5-10-15 rule does not exist. The correct NPPCD standard is the 1-3-6 rule: screen by 1 month of age, confirm diagnosis by 3 months, and begin hearing aid fitting or habilitation by 6 months. Memorise the 1-3-6 rule — it is directly examined.

overallFeedback.feedback: NPPCD was launched in 2006. Its neonatal standard is the 1-3-6 rule: screen by 1 month, diagnose by 3 months, intervene by 6 months. It covers all causes of preventable hearing loss, not NIHL alone.
Correct. NPPCD (2006) + 1-3-6 rule for neonates = the two most examined facts from this programme.
